title: A factor 1.10 efficacy error permits mean half-loss spans above 0.020 in two selected mouse contact models
abstract: We tested whether uncertainty between cleft size and efficacy changes half-weight loss under independent contact failure. We used 1512 Allen V1 Deep Dive and 1438 MICrONS connections with three through eight contacts. Each contact failed with assumed probability 0.1. Its fixed efficacy could range from its size divided by 1.10 to its size multiplied by 1.10. Exact state enumeration gave guaranteed outer mean probability range widths of 0.029907 and 0.028679. Explicit fixed efficacy vectors attained mean spans of 0.021009 and 0.020275. The true widths lie between these values; outer bounds are not claimed sharp. The loss event stayed fixed throughout the efficacy box in 52.1 and 48.1 percent of connections. An independent scalar audit checked all primary connections. One animal per map, partial arbors, assumed rates and errors, and no matched efficacy or activity data limit biological use. Code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and verified external retrieval steps support reproduction. External contact tables and record-level outputs are not bundled.

display.caption: Mean outer and attained half-loss probability widths, certified fractions and count strata. Failure probability is assumed to be 0.1. Ranges describe efficacy uncertainty, not sampling intervals. Outer bounds need not be sharp.
